Hi Alex,

We're working through an RFP and have a short set of technical questions about Redwood's audit logging and retention/export capabilities. Can you please provide answers we can include in the vendor section? If you prefer, a short runbook or sample export would be great. High-level questions below — numbered so we can reference them.

1) Retention windows: what are the default retention periods for audit logs (auth events, API calls, admin actions)? Can customers configure retention per-account or per-route?
2) Exportability: in what formats can audit logs be exported (JSONL, CSV, Parquet, streaming export)? Are exports truncated/aggregated or guaranteed complete for the requested time range?
3) Tamper evidence / integrity: how do you provide proof the logs weren't modified after write (hash chains, signed manifests)?
4) Time fidelity: do logs include event timezone and monotonic sequence numbers for ordering across distributed services?
5) SLA / delivery: typical lead time for on-demand historical exports and any hard limits (size/day) we should expect?
6) Encryption & access controls: how are exported artifacts protected in transit and at rest? Role-based access for export requests?

We're on a tight timeline — any materials you can share by EOD Monday (12 Jan) would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Michael O'Connell
Senior Information Security Manager

Hi Michael — thanks for the clear list. I'm pulling together a concise runbook and a small sample export we can share. Quick answers up front, and I'll follow with the playbook and attachments by Monday: 

1) Retention: default 90 days for high-fidelity audit logs; configurable up to 7 years depending on plan (Hosted/Dedicated/Private). Customers can set account-level retention policies; per-route TTLs supported via policy config.
2) Export formats: JSONL (native), CSV (flattened), Parquet (columnar), and SSE-compatible streaming exports to customer S3/GCS. Exports are complete for the requested range; we include sequence metadata so you can reconcile.
3) Tamper evidence: exports optionally include a signed manifest and SHA256 digests per file; for Dedicated/Private deployments we offer optionally-signed log envelopes using customer-provided KMS keys.
4) Time fidelity: each record includes RFC3339 timestamp, UTC offset, and a monotonic event index propagated from our ingest pipeline for cross-service ordering.
5) SLA/delivery: on-demand exports up to 100GB complete within 24 hours for Hosted; Dedicated customers can request same-day for larger sets via support. We include resumable exports for large ranges.
6) Encryption/access: TLS+HTTPS in transit; AES-256 at rest for Hosted; customer-managed keys for Private. Exports to customer buckets use signed URLs or direct transfer with role-based permissions.

I'll send the playbook + sample export Monday EOD PST. If you'd like a quick call to walk through specifics earlier, I'm available Monday 10–11am or 2–3pm PT.

Best,
Alex Martinez

Hi Michael / Lumina Security,

Thanks for the RFI. Per our internal confirm: attached is a short Playbook (redwood-audit-export-playbook.pdf) and an anonymized sample export (sample-export-20260112.jsonl). Below are point-by-point answers you can paste into the vendor section. If you need a formal signed attestation for the export process we can route through our compliance team.

1) Retention windows
- Hosted: default high-fidelity audit logs retained for 90 days. Customers may purchase extended retention tiers (180 days, 1 year, 2 years) via subscription.
- Dedicated: configurable up to 7 years; typical enterprise customers use 1–3 year windows.
- Private: retention is customer-controlled; policies are enforced by the customer's control plane config.
- Granularity: per-account and per-route TTLs are supported via policy rules; retention policies are applied at ingestion and enforced by lifecycle jobs.

2) Exportability (formats & completeness)
- Supported formats: JSONL (native), CSV (flattened), Parquet (columnar), and streaming export (SSE/Kafka-compatible).
- Completeness: exports are guaranteed complete for the requested time range; export artifacts include sequence metadata (start_seq/end_seq) to aid reconciliation. Large exports use chunked files and a manifest so you can verify all pieces are present.

3) Tamper evidence / integrity
- Signed manifests: exports include a SHA256 digest per file and an overall signed manifest. For Dedicated/Private deployments, we support manifests signed with customer KMS keys (HSM-backed).
- Append-only storage: audit logs are written to append-only storage tiers with immutability flags where requested.

4) Time fidelity & ordering
- Each record contains RFC3339 timestamp, UTC offset, and a monotonic event index propagated across services. We also include an ingestion timestamp. This combination supports deterministic ordering and cross-service reconciliation.

5) SLA / delivery & limits
- Hosted: on-demand exports up to 100GB are typically delivered within 24 hours; larger exports use resumable transfers and are scheduled with support.
- Dedicated: SLA can be configured in the contract for same-day exports and higher throughput.
- We provide resumable export tokens so very large ranges can be resumed from the last successful chunk.

6) Encryption & access control
- In transit: TLS 1.3 for all transfers.
- At rest: AES-256 encryption for Hosted; customer-managed keys (CMK) for Dedicated/Private.
- Export delivery: we support direct push to customer S3/GCS buckets with pre-signed, time-limited URLs or server-to-server transfer authenticated by IAM roles.
- Access controls: RBAC for who may request exports; export requests generate an approval audit trail when requested through the Console or API.
